citations.anchor: throws on duplicate type names
citations.why: Constructing the registry with two types of one name throws — the duplicate-name clause; the registry is built at module construction, so the throw is a boot failure.

citations.anchor: throws when a relation targets an unregistered type
citations.why: The unresolvable-relation-target clause: constructing the registry throws rather than deferring to the first request.

citations.anchor: throws when the inverse targets a non-relation field
citations.why: The unpaired-relationInverse clause: an inverse that does not mirror a real owning relation throws at construction.

citations.anchor: refuses two content types that collide as GraphQL names
citations.why: The GraphQL-name-collision clause: ContentGraphqlPlugin refuses to build at composition time. (Nothing pins that the failure actually aborts `createServer` boot rather than being caught somewhere.)

citations.anchor: does not leak workspace A
citations.why: Listing with workspace B's header returns none of workspace A's entries — the read half of the workspace AND.

citations.anchor: skips an id from another workspace, and does not report it as done
citations.why: The bulk half: a foreign id in a bulk publish is neither written nor counted.

citations.anchor: 404s an entry that lives in another workspace
citations.why: An id from another workspace reads as a 404 on the public read route.

citations.anchor: text: 'Mine now'
citations.why: The write half ('404s an entry in another workspace', the update case): a PATCH addressed at another workspace's entry is a 404, not a cross-workspace write.

citations.anchor: 404s the entries list of an ungranted type with the same body
citations.why: Asserts byte-for-byte body equality (bar the caller-supplied name) between the ungranted and the unknown 404 on the session API. The public REST, GraphQL and tool surfaces only assert the status/code, not the same text, and nothing pins that grants are read before the registry decision.

citations.anchor: rejects a field that collides with an envelope column
citations.why: The declaration half for status; siblings in the same file pin published_at and deleted_at. The 'cannot be set from a request body' half is not pinned on any HTTP surface.

citations.anchor: reserves locale and locale_group_id as field names
citations.why: The two i18n envelope columns cannot be declared as fields.

citations.anchor: saves an incomplete draft of a publishable type, but 422s on publish
citations.why: On a publishable type an incomplete create is a 201 draft and the required check only fires at publish.

citations.anchor: 422s an invalid create of a non-publishable (always-live) type
citations.why: The non-publishable half: the same values are refused on the write itself.

citations.anchor: keeps publishedAt through an edit and clears it on unpublish
citations.why: A save on a published entry returns status draft with publishedAt preserved, and only unpublish clears it.

citations.anchor: saves an incomplete draft of a publishable type, but 422s on publish
citations.why: The publish call carries no body, so the 422 with per-field `issues` can only come from re-validating the stored row. (That the row is still a draft afterwards is not asserted.)

citations.anchor: supersedes the previously-published revision when a newer one publishes
citations.why: After a second publish, v2 is published and v1 is superseded — at most one version live at a time.

citations.anchor: restores an earlier revision as a new revision (append-only)
citations.why: Restoring v1 appends v3 and leaves v1 in place.

citations.anchor: publishes a specific earlier version, making it live
citations.why: Publishing v1 while v3 is newest marks v1 published in place and asserts total is still 3 — no copy is minted.

citations.anchor: appends an incrementing revision on every save, newest first
citations.why: Version numbers increment 1, 2 within one entry. The concurrency half — the advisory lock and the unique-index backstop under two simultaneous writers — is not pinned.

citations.anchor: writes the event in the same transaction as the entry
citations.why: A create rejected inside the write transaction leaves no entry.created outbox/activity row. Pins the row-and-event clause only; the version, the links and the write extensions' state are not shown to roll back with it.

citations.anchor: says nothing when a save changed no value
citations.why: A PATCH resubmitting identical values produces no entry.updated. The bulk half (one event per changed row rather than per id passed) is not pinned — the bulk-delete test passes only ids that are actually removed.

citations.anchor: appends a revision to each sibling the sync rewrote
citations.why: A shared-field change on the source row adds exactly one revision to the sibling the i18n extension rewrote.

citations.anchor: appends exactly one revision when a save moves both a shared field and access
citations.why: The deduplication clause: two extensions reporting the same rewritten row still yield one version for it.

citations.anchor: serves only published, non-deleted entries
citations.why: The default public read excludes drafts and soft-deleted rows.

citations.anchor: lets a write-scoped token read its own draft back
citations.why: ?status=draft and ?status=any are 200 for a write-scoped token and 403 for a read-only one — a guard refusing, not an empty result set.

citations.anchor: never lets a filter widen the published-only scope
citations.why: A filter matching every row still returns only the published one, and `status` is not in the public filter schema at all.

citations.anchor: splits restricted from open
citations.why: An admin session lists a segment-restricted entry with no reader tags — if CONTENT_READ_SCOPE were applied to the admin records list the row would be hidden and the assertion would fail. The 'can only narrow' half is not pinned as such.

citations.anchor: drops a target the reader cannot see from BOTH items and total
citations.why: A relation preview over two links, one unreachable, returns items length 1 and total 1 — the restriction is inside the window and inside the count.

citations.anchor: rejects a target in another locale, naming both sides
citations.why: The one assertSameLocale implementation refuses a cross-locale target when both sides are localized, and is a no-op when either side is not.

citations.anchor: refuses to link two localized types across locales
citations.why: The writer, not the picker: a direct PATCH on the public API is a 422 while the same-locale sibling is accepted. Only the public write path is exercised end to end; the session API and the agent tools are not.

citations.anchor: addresses a write at the group
citations.why: A group-addressed PATCH with ?locale=de rewrites the German row and leaves the English one untouched; taking the locale from body.locale (absent) would have hit the default-locale row.

citations.anchor: 400s a relation delta on a single relation
citations.why: A delta against a field that owns no writable link set is a 400 rather than a silently dropped change.

citations.anchor: 400s a malformed relation delta (non-array unlink), not a 500
citations.why: A structurally malformed delta is rejected at the DTO with a 400. The size bounds on the arrays and on the relations map are not pinned.

citations.anchor: 422s a malformed relation id instead of 500ing
citations.why: A non-uuid relation target comes back as a 422 rather than a Postgres cast error surfacing as a 500.

citations.anchor: returns only the selected fields
citations.why: ?fields= narrows `values` to exactly the named fields while id and publishedAt still come back — the envelope is not selectable away.

citations.anchor: 400s an unknown or unselectable field name
citations.why: An unknown name in ?fields= is a 400.

citations.anchor: reads an empty ?fields= as
citations.why: An empty parameter returns the same full key set as no parameter at all. The 'narrows the SQL projection' clause is not observable from any of these assertions.

citations.anchor: every offered %s path parses against its schema (no drift)
citations.why: The drift test itself: every path the surface offers the picker is parsed against the SQL filter schema from the same walk, so an offered path the API would reject fails the suite.

citations.anchor: keeps the first declarer of a duplicated field name
citations.why: The collision clause: the first declarer of a duplicated virtual field name handles the rule. The workspace-scoping half of the invariant is NOT pinned — no test shows a virtual field's subquery scoped to the workspace passed in.

citations.anchor: omits an ungranted content type from the schema entirely
citations.why: The SDL served to a token omits the ungranted type, so introspection cannot enumerate it.

citations.anchor: gives two workspaces different schemas
citations.why: The schema is per grant set: one token gets different SDL per workspace. The 'TTL is a freshness knob, not a security boundary' clause (revoke, then read before the TTL expires) is not pinned.

citations.anchor: never gives a write input field a default
citations.why: Asserts no mutation input field carries a defaultValue, which is what keeps merge-by-key-presence from becoming overwrite-everything.

citations.anchor: refuses %s over both protocols
citations.why: For three out-of-bounds read arguments, the GraphQL error message is asserted equal to the REST 400's message — the same DTO decorators validated in the resolver.

citations.anchor: pageSize cap
citations.why: The agent-tool half: validateToolInput runs the same DTO, so a tool argument past the cap is refused exactly as the HTTP route refuses it.

citations.anchor: appends a revision, because it went through the ordinary write
citations.why: Applying a copilot change leaves a revision, which only the ordinary EntryWriterService path produces. That the three tool handlers themselves declare effect: 'propose' and write nothing is not asserted.

citations.anchor: offers no tool with a `status` parameter or a publish in its name
citations.why: Walks every offered tool schema: no `status` property and no publish-named tool. The absence of a bulk DELETE tool is not asserted.

citations.anchor: names the sibling locales and the shared field on an edit
citations.why: Editing a shared field on one locale row puts the sibling locale and the field in the proposal summary and in target.fanout.

citations.anchor: refuses a content type the workspace was not granted
citations.why: A propose against an ungranted type is refused with the 'Unknown content type' wording — the same message a non-existent type gives — and under ADR-0009 propose is the apply.

citations.anchor: 403s reading views without content:read
citations.why: A member without content:read cannot read views at all — a saved view is not a way past the permission.

citations.anchor: not 403s — a view addressed from another workspace
citations.why: The workspace half: a view is invisible outside the workspace it was saved in.

citations.anchor: 403s another member editing a shared view
citations.why: The other member is seeded with role 'admin', so this pins 'not even by an administrator' for the edit.

citations.anchor: 403s another member deleting a shared view
citations.why: Same, for delete.

citations.anchor: lets a member default to a shared view they do not own
citations.why: Setting a personal default is not restricted to the owner.

citations.anchor: 403s sharing without views:share, while a private view still saves
citations.why: visibility: 'workspace' needs views:share on create while a private view still saves. That the same check runs on every write (e.g. a PATCH raising visibility) is not pinned.

citations.anchor: 404s an ungranted type exactly as an unknown one
citations.why: A scope naming an ungranted type answers with the same 404 body as an unknown one, resolved through the registry and the grants.

citations.anchor: 404s saving a view over an ungranted type
citations.why: The write side: the endpoint is not a way around ContentGrantGuard.

citations.anchor: never saves, even on a form submit from a field
citations.why: Enter in a text field submits the <form> directly and no save request is issued — runSave returning early, not a disabled button.

citations.anchor: renders every text field read-only, colour field included
citations.why: The 'read-only throughout' half: the fields themselves, not just the actions.

citations.anchor: a failed content-type catalogue leaves the sidebar an error, not an absence
citations.why: A 500 on the type catalogue renders the sidebar error card (with a Try again the next test clicks) rather than removing the navigation.

citations.anchor: a pageSize the server would reject falls back to the default rather than an error card
citations.why: ?pageSize=999 renders rows with no alert — the out-of-range URL parameter degrades instead of stranding the reader in an error card.
